newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch copier maker Oce Q1 net up 62 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch copier maker Oce Q1 net up 62 pct.

text.p: Dutch printer and copier maker Oce on Tuesday said 1996/97 first-quarter net profits rose 62 percent to 44.3 million guilders and said new products would boost its bottom line in the second half.

Turnover in the first quarter to end-February rose 55 percent to 1.20 billion guilders, propelled mainly by last April's acquisition of SNI Printing from Germany's Siemens and the takeover of Messerli of Switzerland, effective January 1.

In the engineering systems segment, Oce said that deliveries of its high volume digital copier Oce 9700 were in full swing. "Particularly during the second half of 1997 the Oce 9700 will make a clear contribution to results," it added.

It said that its office systems unit had built up a large order portfolio for the new Oce 3165, a digital high volume network copier/printer which the company says has gained "excellent market acceptance."
The combined copier/printer was also expected to make a "significant contribution" to results, particularly in the second half of the year, Oce said.

The company gave no fresh earnings forecast for full-year 1997. At the presentation of its 1996 earnings in February it said it expected growth in net profit to outstrip expected full-year sales growth of at least 19.9 percent.
